slides.title: Sample Deck: Schema Conformance Fixture
slides.subtitle: Exercises every layout in presentation2/SCHEMA.md
slides.notes: This is the build's own test fixture, not part of the physics talk. It exists so verify_presentation2.py can build a real deck end to end -- validate, generate a figure, render an equation, emit pptx and html -- without depending on the four content workers' section files, which are written concurrently and may not exist yet.
sources: Synthetic demo content -- schema-conformance fixture, not a literature citation.

slides.title: Bullets layout
bullets: Up to six bullets, each at most about eighteen words long
Plain text bullets render as-is in both the slide deck and the web page
An inline $E=\hbar\omega$ math snippet stays as text, not an image
slides.notes: Demonstrates the plain bullets layout, including the schema's inline-math rule: a bullet that mixes ordinary words with $...$ stays plain text, while a bullet that is only a $...$ expression is rendered as an equation image in the pptx (and as monospace text in the html, since the html renderer never rasterizes math).
sources: Synthetic demo content -- schema-conformance fixture, not a literature citation.

slides.title: Bullets + figure layout
bullets: Bullets on one side, a generated figure on the other
The figure is a PNG produced by a re-runnable, deterministic script
Figures are never downloaded, only generated at build time
slides.notes: Demonstrates the combined bullets+figure layout: bullet text on one side of the slide, the referenced figure and its caption on the other.
sources: Synthetic demo content -- schema-conformance fixture, not a literature citation.

slides.title: Figure-only layout

figure.caption: The same sample figure, shown large with no competing text

slides.notes: Demonstrates the figure-only layout: a large centered figure with a caption and a short title, no bullet text.
sources: Synthetic demo content -- schema-conformance fixture, not a literature citation.

slides.title: Equation layout

equations.caption: photon energy; hbar reduced Planck constant, omega angular frequency
decay rate; tau spontaneous emission lifetime

slides.notes: Demonstrates the equation layout: each equation is rendered by mathimg.py to a cached PNG and placed as a picture with its caption beneath it, up to three equations per slide.
sources: Synthetic demo content -- schema-conformance fixture, not a literature citation.

slides.title: Data-driven slides keep four concurrent writers from stepping on one renderer's toes.
slides.subtitle: Demo callout -- no attribution, schema-conformance fixture only

slides.title: Provenance footnote demo
bullets: This slide carries a repo_numbers entry
The renderer prints it as a small provenance footnote
The validator checks the value against the named file
slides.notes: Demonstrates repo_numbers: the value below is checked by validate_sections.py against out/rt_edge/verdict.md (it must appear in that file as a numeric token within 1e-6), and both renderers print a provenance footnote citing the source file.
